questions.question: In the shortest path binary formulation with origin $s$, destination $t$ and edge lengths $\ell_{ij}$, what does $x_{ij}=1$ mean?
options: The route passes through both vertices $i$ and $j$
The directed edge from $i$ to $j$ is selected for the route
The undirected edge $\{i,j\}$ is used in either direction
The shortest distance from $i$ to $j$ equals $\ell_{ij}$

questions.question: The course shortest path problem is set on an undirected network. Why does the binary formulation create both directed orientations $x_{ij}$ and $x_{ji}$ of each edge $\{i,j\}$?
options: Each edge's length must be charged once per direction
The route has to come back from $t$ to the origin $s$
Each edge then appears in two of the balance constraints
A route may need to cross the edge in either direction

questions.question: In the shortest path binary formulation with origin $s$ and destination $t$, the balance at every other vertex $i$ is $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}=0$. What does this say about a selected route?
options: Vertex $i$ lies on no selected route at all
As many selected edges leave $i$ as enter it
At most one selected edge may touch vertex $i$
Vertex $i$ has as many incident edges as neighbours

questions.question: Consider a feasible solution of the shortest path binary formulation (origin $s$, destination $t$, edge lengths $\ell_{ij}>0$) whose selected edges form a single route from $s$ to $t$. What does $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ equal?
options: The number of edges on the selected route
The length of the single longest edge on the route
The total length of all edges in the network
The total length of the selected route's edges

questions.question: In the shortest path binary formulation (origin $s$, destination $t$), a vertex $v$ is not on the selected route and the solution contains no cycle. Which statement about $v$ is correct?
options: Its balance constraint must be removed from the model
One of the variables at $v$ must still equal 1
Its variables are all 0 and its balance reads $0=0$
Its balance has right-hand side $-1$ instead of 0

questions.question: An undirected network has 5 vertices and 7 edges. How many binary variables $x_{ij}$ does its shortest path binary formulation have, with one per directed orientation of an existing edge?

A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin $s=A$ and destination $t=E$. In the binary formulation (minimize $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ equal to $1$ at $s$, $-1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$), which is the balance constraint at B?
options: $x_{BA}+x_{BC}+x_{BD}-x_{AB}-x_{CB}-x_{DB}=0$
$x_{BA}+x_{BC}+x_{BD}+x_{AB}+x_{CB}+x_{DB}=2$
$x_{BA}+x_{BC}+x_{BD}-x_{AB}-x_{CB}-x_{DB}=1$

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin A and destination E, and directed variables $x_{ij}$ for both orientations of each edge. Which variables equal 1 for the route A-C-B-D-E?
options: $x_{AC},x_{BC},x_{BD},x_{DE}$
$x_{CA},x_{BC},x_{DB},x_{ED}$
$x_{AB},x_{BD},x_{DE}$
$x_{AC},x_{CB},x_{BD},x_{DE}$

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin A and destination E. In the binary formulation (minimize $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ equal to $1$ at $s$, $-1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$), a student sets $x_{AC}=x_{CB}=x_{CD}=x_{DE}=1$ and all other variables to 0. Which balance constraints fail?
options: None; all four edges exist
Those at vertices B and C
Only the one at vertex C
Those at vertices C and D

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin $s=A$ and destination $t=E$. What is the optimal objective value of the binary formulation (minimize $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ equal to $1$ at $s$, $-1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$)?

In the shortest path binary formulation with origin $s$ and destination $t$, the right-hand sides $1$ at $s$ and $-1$ at $t$ are changed to $2$ and $-2$, with positive edge lengths and $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$. What does the model then select?
options: The shortest route twice, with each of its variables equal to 2
Nothing: a binary $x_{ij}$ cannot carry two units of flow
Two $s$-$t$ routes sharing no directed edge, of least total length
The two shortest $s$-$t$ routes, even if they share directed edges

questions.question: In the shortest path binary formulation with nonnegative edge lengths, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ is replaced by $0\le x_{ij}\le1$ (the LP relaxation). Which statement is correct?
options: Some optimal solution is integral, so the value is the shortest length
Every optimal solution is a single path, so the relaxation is exact
Its value is a lower bound that may lie strictly below the shortest length
Its value is half the shortest length, using $x_{ij}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.question: The course shortest path problem assumes nonnegative edge lengths. In the binary formulation of an undirected network, what would go wrong if one edge $\{u,v\}$ had length $-3$?
options: The balance constraints would have no feasible solution
The edge could only be crossed in the direction from $u$ to $v$
$x_{uv}=x_{vu}=1$ can add a cycle of length $-6$ to a route
The binary restriction would make that edge's variable negative

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin A and destination E. A modeller creates only the orientation from the alphabetically earlier vertex ($x_{AB}$, $x_{BC}$, …) and solves the binary formulation. What optimal value does this flawed model give?

A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, with origin A and destination E. In the binary formulation (minimize $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ equal to $1$ at $s$, $-1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$), consider $x_{AB}=x_{BD}=x_{DE}=x_{BC}=x_{CB}=1$, all other variables 0. Which statement is correct?
options: Infeasible, as B has two edges in and two out
Feasible, with objective value 13
Feasible, with objective value 11
Infeasible, as $x_{BC}$ and $x_{CB}$ are both 1

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 3, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2, origin A, destination E. In the LP relaxation ($0\le x_{ij}\le1$) of the binary formulation, is $x_{AB}=x_{AC}=x_{CB}=\frac{1}{2}$, $x_{BD}=x_{DE}=1$, others 0, optimal?
options: No: B receives flow on two edges, breaking its balance
No: its value 10.5 exceeds the shortest route length
Yes: it is feasible with value 10, the shortest length
Yes: its value 5 lies strictly below the binary optimum

questions.question: In the shortest path binary formulation with origin $s$, destination $t$ and strictly positive edge lengths, why does an optimal solution contain no unnecessary cycle?
options: Deleting a cycle keeps every balance and strictly lowers the cost
The balance constraints rule out every directed cycle
Binary variables cannot select edges that form a cycle
A cycle would make the route visit $t$ twice, breaking its balance

questions.question: For the shortest path binary formulation with origin $s$ and destination $t$, a student writes the balances $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ with right-hand side $1$ at $s$, $1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere. What happens?
options: No $x$ is feasible: summing all balances gives $0=2$
It finds the shortest route from $t$ back to $s$
It finds the same shortest route, as edges are undirected
It selects one route leaving $s$ and another leaving $t$

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 2, B-D 3, A-C 4, C-D 2 and C-E 0, with origin A and destination D. In the binary formulation (minimize $\sum\ell_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_jx_{ij}-\sum_jx_{ji}$ equal to $1$ at $s$, $-1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$), $x_{AB}=x_{BD}=1$ (others 0) is optimal. Which other vector is also optimal?
options: $x_{AB}=x_{BD}=x_{CE}=1$, others 0
$x_{AC}=x_{CE}=x_{EC}=x_{CD}=1$, others 0
$x_{AB}=x_{BD}=x_{DC}=x_{CD}=1$, others 0
$x_{AB}=x_{BD}=x_{CE}=x_{EC}=1$, others 0

questions.question: A network has edges A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C $L$, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10 and D-E 2 with $L\ge0$, origin A and destination E. For which $L$ is $x_{AC}=x_{CB}=x_{BD}=x_{DE}=1$, others 0, an optimal solution of the binary formulation?
options: $0\le L\le3$
$0\le L\le11$
$0\le L\le2$
